ca_bankrupt_wall.blurb: Bankrupt Wall is a small west-facing cliff in the Wonderland of Rocks section of Joshua Tree National Park. It stands beside the wash, north of the Previously Unreleased Material wall, tucked behind shrubs at a bend, so it is easy to walk past. The monzogranite is solid, and the lines are short, with funky moves rather than the usual crack climbing; several need a stretch of unprotected slab to reach the start. Seven routes include five trad leads and two top-rope problems, from 5.6 up to 5.11a, with most at 5.10 or easier. A ramp at the left end of the formation serves for walking off or rigging top ropes.

ca_bart_dome.blurb: Bart Dome is a south-facing granodiorite dome in the Domeland Wilderness of the southern Sierra Nevada, rising roughly 800 feet. Dikes and water grooves run across the face, which is heavily featured and mostly a little off vertical. Seven routes climb it, mainly multi-pitch alpine-style trad lines plus one bolted line, with grades from 5.7 to 5.12 and the bulk around 5.10. The face warms up over the day, though a breeze often helps. Water on the way in dries up late in the season, and the hike to the base is long, so it suits a committed outing rather than a quick stop.

ca_bay_tree_boulders.blurb: Bay Tree Boulders is a group of seven problems in Upper Cold Springs Canyon above Santa Barbara, set in a shaded wooded stretch along the west fork trail. The grades run from V1 to V7, with most between V2 and V5, so moderate boulderers have plenty to try and one hard line tops the range. The sandstone is very solid, with slopers and crimps on the problems. The boulders sit right beside the path, so hikers pass through, though the walk in is long enough to keep crowds lighter than in the lower canyon. Poison oak grows widely around the landings.

ca_belafonte_the.blurb: The Belafonte is a single large boulder with a deep diagonal gash, part of the Jah Hole section of the Brickyard, Santa Barbara's sandstone bouldering zone. Seven problems range from V0 to V6, most between V1 and V4. Lower-angle slabs on the right suit warm-ups and slab technique, while taller and harder lines sit on the left, including a pair of traverses. Recent cleaning uncovered more slab lines and a crimpy problem, and the surface collects dust and lichen, so bring a brush and a few pads.

ca_big_rocks.blurb: Big Rocks is a sport crag in the Hwy 166/Silly Rock area on California's Central Coast, farther up the main track than Owl Tor. The centerpiece is a large dome with big caves. Seven sport routes run from 5.8 to 5.10, and over half are 5.10, so it suits climbers comfortable at that level. The conglomerate varies from poor to good, with loose pieces here and there, which makes a helmet a good idea. Summer heat makes it a poor choice then; other crags nearby are better in that season.

ca_blackhawk_pinnacle.blurb: Blackhawk Pinnacle is a small crag in the San Bernardino Mountains, at roughly 6,000 feet in the Cactus Flats area off Highway 18 between Big Bear and Lucerne Valley. Routes are only 40 to 50 feet tall. Seven lines, mostly trad with one sport route, range from 5.7 to 5.12, and most fall between 5.8 and 5.10. The granodiorite is very good in places and a little gritty or lichen-covered in others. It makes a short stop for a few leads.

ca_backside_boulder.blurb: Backside Boulder is part of Boulder Gulch in the Kern Valley of the southern Sierra, over the hill from Campground 61. A short walk up the main trail leads to the main boulder, which is brownish with a prominent arcing crack across its face. Seven problems run from V0 to V7, mostly V1 through V4, with one hard outlier, so a range of abilities find something. The granodiorite is high quality and there is plenty of afternoon sun, which suits cooler months.
